title: fix(plugin-timeline): a gantt-variant timeline draws its headers and bars on one continuous axis (objectui#11079)
body:
Fixes #11079
Clause-②: no

## What was wrong

A `variant: 'gantt'` timeline built its header row and its bars from two different constructions in `packages/plugin-timeline/src/renderer.tsx`:

- `generateTimeScaleHeaders` drew one equal-width `flex-1` column per unit, from the minimum date to the maximum date inclusive;
- `calculateBarDimensions` placed each bar as a percentage of the span from the minimum date to the maximum date, which ends at the START of the last column.

So the bars sat on a scale one column narrower than the headers. On a day axis over October 5th to 7th, the bar starting on the 6th was drawn at `left: 50%` under a column that starts at one third.

## What this changes (triage `5888963850`: one continuous axis)

- **One axis function.** The new module-private `timelineAxis(scale, minDate, maxDate, locale, t)` returns `{ start, end, units: [{ start, end, label }] }`. The axis is `[start of the first unit, end of the last unit)`: the first unit contains `minDate`, and the last unit contains `maxDate`.
- **One placement function.** `placeOnAxis(axis, start, end)` returns `{ start, width }` as percentages of the axis span. Each header cell's `width` and each bar's `left` / `width` come from this call. There is no second construction.
- **Each header is as wide as its unit's real length.** `hour` steps a fixed hour. `day`, `week`, `month`, `quarter` and `year` step with local setters from a local midnight. So day and hour columns are equal, a month is as wide as its days, and a DST day is 23 or 25 hours wide.
- **Units snap to their boundary.** The old walk stepped from `minDate` itself. So a month axis from January 15th to April 10th had no April column, and one from January 31st skipped February. `week` still counts from the axis's first day, as its `Week N` labels always did.
- **The inverted-range refusal is the axis's own refusal.** The branch used to run a separate greater-than test "deliberately the same test `generateTimeScaleHeaders` makes". It now refuses when `timelineAxis` builds no axis: the same read.
- **Dates are still read through `readGanttDate`**, the objectui#10866 slice-3 invariant. No date read changes.
- `generateTimeScaleHeaders` keeps its exported signature and now returns the axis's labels. No export, prop, type or schema key is added or removed.
- The header cells' `flex-1` becomes `shrink-0 min-w-0 overflow-hidden` plus an inline percentage `width`. That keeps a long label from widening its column off the bars.

## Pins

New: `packages/plugin-timeline/src/__tests__/TimelineGantt.oneAxis-11079.test.tsx`, with 25 cases.

- For each of the six spec scales, on a pinned three-unit range:
  - a bar starting at the second unit's start has `left` equal, as a string, to the first header's `width`;
  - that bar is exactly as wide as the second header;
  - a bar spanning the last unit ends at 100% (`left + width`, to 10 decimal places);
  - the header widths match each unit's length.
- `month` across a 28/31-day boundary (January 2026, then February): the widths are 31/90 and 28/90.
- The card's own computed day axis: the Oct 6 bar sits at one third, not 50%.
- The three unit-boundary cases above.
- The schema catalog's `gantt-style-timeline.json`, read from disk as the named real producer: months at 31/121, 29/121, 31/121 and 30/121. Implementation starts on the Feb header, and QA Phase on the Mar header.

`TimelineGantt.dateOnlyZone-10866.test.tsx` gets one new driven case, run in Los Angeles: a day axis across the March 8th 2026 spring change. Its columns are 24/71, 23/71 and 24/71, and a bar from March 8th starts on its column. The zone-pin driver `scripts/__tests__/date-only-zone-pins-10183.test.ts` already lists this file, so its PINS list needed no change.

Re-derived from the new axis, each with a comment naming objectui#11079 and its day-count derivation. Zone-rule assertions are untouched:

- `TimelineGantt.dateOnlyZone-10866.test.tsx`: the computed-range and pinned-mixed bars, in the suite zone and both driven zones. A header-width read was added so the pinned day bar can be compared with its column.
- `timeline-gantt-empty-items.test.tsx`: pin 4 (the catalog shape on 91 days) and pin 5b (see Acceptance notes).
- `timeline-gantt-unusable-date-range.test.tsx`: the degenerate pinned range and the healthy-path pin.
- `timeline-gantt-null-date-6770.test.tsx` and `timeline-gantt-date-type-rule-6781.test.tsx`: their bar-geometry pins. The dispatch did not list these two files, but they read the same geometry.

## Evidence (objectui HEAD `efee2d5bd`, base `88fbd793d`)

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-timeline/`: `Test Files 37 passed (37)`, `Tests 389 passed | 32 skipped (421)`. The base read 36 files, 364 passed and 31 skipped. The 25 new cases are all counted as passed; the new DST case is a driven case, so the normal run skips it.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-timeline type-check` exits 0. `tsconfig.test.json` includes all six touched test files, counted with `--listFiles`.
- In one run, four files pass (`Tests 660 passed (660)`): the zone driver `scripts/__tests__/date-only-zone-pins-10183.test.ts` (27 passed; the forked child ran every case of every pin, including the new DST case), `examples/schema-catalog/test/catalog-gallery-render.test.tsx` (587 passed), and the two `packages/types` tests that read `plugin-timeline.mdx` (46 passed).
- eslint on the 7 changed `.ts`/`.tsx` files (`--format json`: 7 files): 0 errors and 34 warnings. The same 6 pre-existing files read 34 warnings on the base, and the new file has 0. The narrowing is safe: `eslint.config.js` enables no type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project` / `projectService`), and no custom rule under `eslint-rules/` reads the filesystem. So this diff cannot move the verdict of any untouched file. The full `pnpm lint` run is CI's.
- These gates exit 0: `check-changeset-presence`, `check-control-bytes`, `check-new-cross-file-line-citations` (0 new), `check-changeset-claims`, `check-pending-changeset-literals`, `check-test-path-roots`, `check-i18n-call-site-keys`, `check-unreferenced-sources`, `check-changeset-no-major` and `check-doc-fence-languages`. `check-governed-queue-guard --test` reports NOT GOVERNED.
- **Reverse verification (one time, not kept).** With the fix committed, `renderer.tsx` was put back to the base blob, and the mutation was confirmed on disk (`function timelineAxis` 0 hits). The six touched test files then read `Tests 38 failed | 63 passed | 14 skipped`, and 24 of the 25 new cases went red; only the fixture-on-disk check stayed green. The file was then restored with `git checkout HEAD --`. The restore is proven by its blob hash matching `HEAD` and by an empty `git diff HEAD`. The direction was red, as predicted.
- **Real layout engine.** The rendered gantt was laid out in Chromium at 1200px, using the Tailwind utilities it uses written out by hand, not the app's built stylesheet:
  - the card's Oct 6 bar starts at x 528.328, the Oct 6 header's x;
  - in the catalog gantt, Implementation starts at 450.734, the Feb header's x, and QA Phase at 691.828, the Mar header's x.

## Acceptance notes

- **Inline `width` on the header cells.** AGENTS.md §2 bans inline styles outside the colour carve-out. `skills/objectui/rules/styling.md` says a runtime geometry value "is a separate question this carve-out does not answer". The header width follows `TimelineGanttBar`'s existing inline `left` / `width`, which is the same kind of value. The Zone 2 guidance asked for inline percentage widths. A computed percentage cannot be a static utility.
- **Pin 5b moved from a full-width bar to a zero-width one.** Before, a plan whose only dates were one same-day task (`2024-05-01` to `2024-05-01`) drew its bar at `left: 0%; width: 100%`. That value was the `totalDuration === 0` special case. Now the axis always spans at least one whole unit, so the guard had nothing left to catch and was removed. The bar is `left: 0%; width: 0%`, as a zero-length task already was on any plan with two distinct dates. The pinned `minDate === maxDate` case is now a one-unit axis, and the bar overhangs it the way any bar outside a pinned range does. This is recorded in the changeset.
- **Out of scope, reported for the seat.** The catalog's producer writes inclusive date-only ends (API Design `2024-01-01` to `2024-01-31`), but `readGanttDate` reads an end as the instant it names (local midnight at the start of that day). So each such bar now ends visibly one day short of its month column, and a same-day task is invisible. Before this change, the equal-width columns hid the one-day gap by coincidence. The claim forbids changing how a date is read, so this is left for its own card.
- **Also outside the claimed file surface:** one sentence in `content/docs/plugins/plugin-timeline.mdx` ("Time Scales (Gantt)") describes the shared axis, per AGENTS.md #2.
